content.text:
Yes—all three findings are closed **at the delivery-contract level**. I found no remaining substantive gaps in these fixes.

1. **Maiden navigation:** The mandatory patch follows directory symlinks with explicit errors; acceptance requires actual root-to-application tree navigation, editing, saving and execution of that same file, excluding direct-URL shortcuts (`docs/delivery/completions/H00.md:101–112`). This addresses the actual mismatch between launcher symlinks (`src/runtime/native.py:103`) and Maiden’s `entry.IsDir()` check (`.runtime/h00/maiden/cmd/server.go:911`).

2. **Persistence:** Explicit owned-dataset reopening, independent dataset identity, single-writer locking, preserved application files and a generated-file allowlist address the current fresh-per-session allocation (`src/automation/session.py:52–59`). Recreated-container acceptance requires restored behavior without reseeding (`docs/delivery/completions/H00.md:125–140`).

3. **REPL recovery:** Visible diagnostics followed by owned-session restart, dataset reopening, relay replacement and editor reconnection provide a coherent recovery path. Corrected-command, controls and actual-audio checks establish usability afterward; injected genuine engine failures must remain explicit failures (`docs/delivery/completions/H00.md:113–124`). This accommodates the existing sticky error behavior (`src/runtime/native.py:246–264`).

**CONFIDENCE: High.** Implementation and passing acceptance remain unverified and explicitly pending (`docs/delivery/reviews/H00-triage.md:17–19`); this closes the plan findings, not runtime admission.
